source.what: Joby Aviation single news-article page (the BLADEone / Aero jet-service announcement) — a full rubric covering all seven aspects, not just structure. Captured from the live page at three viewports plus targeted probes for type, spacing, colour, imagery, motion and copy.
source.method: Chromium (ms-playwright chromium-1234) driven by puppeteer-core, one isolated browser context per width, so no state leaks between passes. Viewports 1440x900, 834x1112, 390x844 at deviceScaleFactor 1. Each pass scrolled once through the document to trigger reveals, then every running animation was finished and its styles committed so nothing measured was stuck in a hidden pre-animation state (verified: hiddenAfterFinish 1, that one being the cookie banner). Cookie and page-transition overlays were removed from the DOM before measurement — the page-transition layer is what hides the footer in a naive full-page capture. All numbers are getComputedStyle and getBoundingClientRect readings plus resolved :root custom properties, never estimates.
gaps: The pull-quote is measured as it is: there is no blockquote element on the page and no oversized quotation style. Two quoted passages sit inside ordinary 16px body paragraphs using curly quotes. The rubric records that absence rather than inventing a quote treatment, and the 'attribute a quotation' move is written as a corrected contract, flagged as not present on the source.

Paragraph separation is produced by
elements (each exactly one line-height tall, 19px) rather than by margins. Measured p-to-p distance is 38px, which is two line-heights: one for the
and one for the gap. The authoring intent (a line break standing in for paragraph spacing) is inferred from the DOM order, not from a declaration.

The hero image's vertical offset is confirmed at 202.5px (its container is 900px tall, the image renders 1035px tall and is cropped by overflow), but whether the composition offset is authored or an artifact of object-position was not resolved.

The media section's 1.6:1 aspect is enforced by the section's own height (900px against 1440px width), not by the image element, which renders at 1.39:1 and is cropped. Which element owns the aspect was not isolated.

The 'Read next' card row's alignment failure is characterised precisely (image tops at 4238.1 / 4321.9 / 4410.4, a 172.3px spread, driven by unequal heading heights above the images) but the page's intended fix is not recorded anywhere on the source, so the corrected contract is the rubric author's construction.

Motion was sampled after the reveal had completed at 1440 only; the entrance stagger across the three news cards and the hero's word-level animation are inferred from the shared keyframe library and the captured early-sampling data, not measured per element.
Hover and focus states on body links, the rail's share buttons and the 'View all News' button were read from authored CSS; only the button's colour transition was captured live.

The sidebar rail is measured as position relative in the captured state, with its sticky behaviour not exercised. The rail's 1732px height against the article's 1044px content height suggests the sticky wrapper is authored, but that was not confirmed by scrolling.

The footer and nav are site-wide components with their own rubrics (joby_nav_v1.json, joby_footer_v1.json). They are described here only as they appear on this page, and their internals are not re-graded.
source.notes: This page's headline finding is that it uses ONE grid definition everywhere — hero, media band, article, sidebar, Read next and footer are all the same 16-column, 16px-gap, 40px-gutter grid, at 1440 measuring exactly 16x70 + 15x16 + 80 = 1440. The commonly reported fault ('the blog grid does not match the footer grid') is false as stated: the grids are identical. The real defect is that the same 16 tracks carry two incompatible placement systems — the article and Read next place children by column span, while the Read next card row abandons columns entirely for flex content widths (559 / 458 / 343), and the footer leaves columns 3-10 undeclared. Three further defects are recorded as negative evidence: the card row's 172.3px image-top spread, paragraph spacing produced by line-break elements rather than a rhythm, and a triple column system across breakpoints (16 fixed-px tracks, then a 100px-gap fluid variant at 1024, then 6 tracks at 600).

parts.name: One grid, every section
parts.description: Hero, media band, standfirst, article, sidebar, Read next and footer are all the same 16-column grid with the same 16px column gap and the same 40px page gutter. At 1440 the tracks are fixed 70px columns and the arithmetic closes exactly: 16 columns of 70px plus 15 gaps of 16px plus two 40px gutters equals 1440. The tracks are px, not fractions, so the gutter absorbs any viewport change rather than the columns.
parts.entry_test: Give any one section its own grid definition and the page's left edges stop agreeing across section boundaries; the single shared definition is what makes the headline, the body and the section label all start at the same x.
parts.recipe: Declare the grid once on a shared token set and consume it in every section: grid-template-columns repeat(var(--grid-columns), 1fr) is NOT what this page does — it fixes the tracks in px and lets the gutter carry the load. At 1440: 16 tracks of 70px, column-gap 16px, padding 0 40px, giving a 1360px content band (1120px of tracks + 240px of gaps). The same 16/16/40 system appears in the hero, the media band, the standfirst, the article, the sidebar, Read next and the footer with no per-section overrides. Do not let a section declare its own columns or its own gutter.

checks.check: Every section resolves to the same column count, gap and gutter
The track arithmetic closes exactly against the viewport width
Tracks are fixed px (or an equivalent scale), not free fractions
No section declares a private grid definition
The gutter, not the columns, absorbs viewport change

evidence: measured at 1440: all five grid containers resolve to '70px' x16, columnGap 16px, padding 0 40px
arithmetic closes: 16x70 + 15x16 = 1120 + 240 = 1360 = 1440 - 80, exact
SectionNews computed gridTemplateColumns '70px 70px ... 70px' (16 entries), gap 16px
at 1200 tracks are 55px and at 1024 they are 44px, with the gap held at 16px and the gutter at 40px in all three cases
the footer grid resolves to the same 16 tracks, 16px gap, 40px gutter as every content section

parts.name: Place children by span, not by content width
parts.description: The article's blocks are placed by explicit column spans on the shared grid: the headline spans 12 columns, the caption spans 8, the published block runs from column 9 to the end, the sidebar rail spans 2, and the article measure spans 8 starting at column 5. Nothing in the reading column is sized by its own content. This is the page's dominant placement system and the one the Read next card row breaks.
parts.entry_test: Size the reading column to its own content and the measure stops being constant across the article; the fixed span is what holds the measure at exactly eight tracks regardless of what the text says.
parts.recipe: Place every reading-column block with an explicit grid-column: h1 1 / span 12; hero caption 1 / span 8; published block 9 / -1; standfirst 5 / -1; sidebar rail span 2; article content 5 / span 8. At 1440 these resolve to h1 x 40 w 1016, caption x 40 w 672, published x 728 w 672, standfirst x 384 w 1016, rail x 40 w 156, article x 384 w 672. Note that this page uses a deliberately small span vocabulary — 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 12 and the -1 rail — and reuses it across sections. Do not place a major block by its own text width.

checks.check: Reading-column blocks are placed by column span, not content width
The article measure resolves to a constant span across the whole article
The sidebar rail occupies its own span, separate from the measure
The span vocabulary stays small and is reused between sections
The headline's span is visibly wider than the article measure

evidence: measured: h1 gridColumn '1 / span 12' -> x 40 w 1016; article content '5 / span 8' -> x 384 w 672; rail 'span 2' -> x 40 w 156
h1 renders 1016px wide against the body's 672px — a 1.51x difference inside one section stack
standfirst spans to the -1 rail (x 384 w 1016) while the article beneath it narrows to span 8
span vocabulary in use on this page: 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 12, 16 and the -1 end rail

parts.name: Full-bleed media band
parts.description: The hero image is a full-bleed band, edge to edge with no gutter, no radius and no border, and it is the only element on the page that escapes the 40px gutter. It is cropped by an overflow container so the visible composition is a 1440x900 window onto a taller image.
parts.entry_test: Inset the media band to the content gutter and the page's rhythm breaks at exactly the point the eye expects air; the full-bleed band is what separates the headline block from the article.
parts.recipe: A full-width section, height 900px at 1440 (a 1.6:1 band), overflow hidden, holding an image at object-fit cover with border-radius 0. The image itself renders larger than its container (1656x1035 against a 1440x900 box, offset -108px left and 202.5px down) and is cropped by the container's overflow. Keep the band out of the grid's padding — it spans the full viewport while every other block is inset by 40px. There is a 16px margin below the band before the standfirst begins.

checks.check: The media band spans the full viewport, escaping the page gutter
The band has no border radius or border
The image is cropped to the band rather than letterboxed
The band is the only full-bleed element above the footer
The band holds a fixed aspect rather than an arbitrary height

evidence: measured: mediaSection box x 0 w 1440 h 900; img box x -108 w 1656 h 1035 — the image overflows and is cropped
computed border-radius '0px' on both the section and the image; object-fit 'cover'
natural image size 1600x1200 (1.33:1) rendered into a 1.6:1 band
section margin '0px 0px 16px' — a 16px gap before the standfirst band
no other element above the footer spans x 0 w 1440

parts.name: Standfirst band wider than the article
parts.description: A summary line sits in its own full-width band between the media and the article, set at 24px display type across a 1016px measure — wider than the 672px article it introduces. The band is not inset to the article's column; it starts at column 5 and runs to the right rail.
parts.entry_test: Set the standfirst at the article's measure and the page loses its entry point; the wider measure and the display face are what mark the summary as a different order of text from the body.
parts.recipe: A section spanning the full width with its text block placed at 5 / -1 on the shared grid (x 384 w 1016 at 1440), set in the display face at 24px weight 500, line-height 28.8px, tracking -0.24px. The band itself is 211.1px tall at 1440 and sits directly below the media band's 16px margin. Keep the summary measure wider than the article measure; do not align the two to the same right edge as if they were one column.

checks.check: The standfirst sits in its own band between media and article
Its measure is wider than the article measure below it
It is set in the display face, not the body face
Its size is between the headline and the body, not equal to either
It is a single summary, not a paragraph run

evidence: measured: band box x 0 y 1769.1 w 1440 h 211.1; text block x 384 w 1016
computed on the summary: 24px/500, line-height 28.8px (1.2), letter-spacing -0.24px, font-family jobyDisplay
the article below it is 672px wide — the summary is 1.51x the body measure
gap from the media band: 16px (the media section's bottom margin)

parts.name: Reading measure beside a fixed rail
parts.description: The article's text occupies columns 5 through 12 — eight tracks, 672px at 1440 — while a narrow 156px rail sits on columns 1-2 carrying the published date and the share controls. The rail is empty of body text and the measure never widens to fill it.
parts.entry_test: Let the body run the full band and the measure becomes a 1360px slog; the 672px span is what sets the reading rhythm.
parts.recipe: content at grid-column 5 / span 8 on the shared grid; the rail at span 2. At 1440 the measure is exactly 672px = 8 tracks + 7 gaps. The rail's own box measures 156px wide and 1732px tall — taller than the 1044px of article content it sits beside, because it is inside a sticky wrapper; the rail is authored to travel with the scroll. Keep the measure at the 672px span and do not let it absorb the rail's columns when the rail is present.

checks.check: The article measure resolves to a constant 8-track span
A narrow rail holds the metadata and share controls in its own span
The measure does not widen to fill the rail's columns
Approximate characters per line falls in a readable band, not a 1360px band
The rail is vertically offset from the article's top rather than baseline-aligned to it

evidence: measured: article content box x 384 w 672 h 1044; rail box x 40 w 156 h 1732
672px = 8 tracks of 70px + 7 gaps of 16px, exact
at 16px type the 672px measure carries roughly 84 characters, a long but bounded measure; the full band would be roughly 170
rail contents: 'Published October 2 2026' plus four controls labelled Copy Link, Facebook, LinkedIn, X

parts.name: One paragraph rhythm, top to bottom
parts.description: This is a negative move recording a defect. Paragraph separation on the page is produced by break elements rather than by a declared spacing value: each paragraph is separated by a br that is exactly one line-height tall, so the visual gap between paragraphs is a line break rather than a rhythm step. The result is that paragraph spacing is tied to line-height and cannot be tuned independently of type size.
parts.entry_test:
Not a gesture to copy — the opposite. Recorded because a full rubric that omits it will reproduce a page whose paragraph rhythm is an accident of
elements. Paragraph spacing must be a declared value, and must survive a change of type size.
parts.recipe: Replace break-element separation with a declared paragraph gap. On this page each of the six paragraphs is followed by a br rendering 19px tall (one line-height at 16px with normal leading), and paragraph-to-paragraph distance measures 38px — two line-heights, one for the break and one for the gap. There is no margin or padding on any paragraph (computed margin 0px, padding 0px on all six). The correct contract: set paragraph margin-bottom from the spacing ladder so the gap is a chosen value, and let line-height govern leading only. Do not use br as a layout device.

checks.check: Paragraph separation is a declared margin or gap, not a break element
Paragraph spacing is independent of the line-height
Every paragraph carries the same spacing value
Changing the type size does not change the paragraph gap proportionally
No paragraph is separated by a different mechanism than its siblings

evidence: measured DOM order in mainContent: p, br, p, br, p, br, p, br, p, br, p — five breaks between six paragraphs
each br computes 16px/400 with line-height normal and renders exactly 19px tall
paragraph-to-paragraph distance is 38px = 19px break + 19px leading
computed margin and padding are 0px on every one of the six paragraphs

parts.name: Read next band, full content width
parts.description: The Read next section is an edge-to-edge band on the page's canvas colour, holding a section label at columns 1-7 and a 'View all News' control at columns 14-16, with the card row spanning the full 16 columns beneath them.
parts.entry_test: Inset the section label to the article's measure and the page loses its section break; the label returning to column 1 is what marks the article as finished.
parts.recipe: A full-width band on the canvas colour with padding 23px 40px 57px (note the asymmetry: 23px top, 57px bottom, neither from a scale). Its label sits at 1 / span 7 and the control at 14 / span 3; the card container spans 1 / span 16. At 1440: label x 40 w 586, control x 1257.1 w 142.9 h 38.9, container x 40 w 1360. The control is a text button with no background, no radius and no border, transitioning colour over 0.3s on cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1).

checks.check: The band spans the full content width, not the article measure
The label returns to column 1 and the control sits at the right rail
The label and control are separated by empty interior columns
The band's background matches the page canvas rather than introducing a new surface
The control carries no container, background or border

evidence: measured: SectionNews box x 0 y 3898.2 w 1440 h 808.9, padding '23px 40px 57px', display grid on 16 x 70px tracks, gap 16px
h2 'Read next' at 64px/550/-1.92px; box x 40 w 586
control box x 1257.1 w 142.9 h 38.9, computed background rgba(0,0,0,0), border-radius 0px, transition 'color 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1)'

parts.name: Cards placed on tracks, not content widths
parts.description: This is a negative move recording the page's central defect. The card row is dropped onto a 16-track grid but ignores it: the three cards are flex children sized by their own content, measuring 559, 458 and 343px, so no card edge except the first and last aligns to a track. Card 2 begins at x 599, which is not a track start.
parts.entry_test: Not a gesture to copy — the opposite. A card row on a 16-column grid must place its cards by span; this row is the reason the page reads as two incompatible placement systems sharing one grid.
parts.recipe: Place the cards by explicit span on the same 16 tracks the label above them uses. As authored, the three newsItem elements are laid out by flex with content-derived widths — 559 / 458 / 343px at 1440, a 1.63:1 ratio between the first two — so their interior edges fall between tracks (card 2 starts at x 599; the nearest track starts are 560 at the end of column 8 and 646 at the start of column 10). The row is flushed to both rails (x 40 to x 1400) while its interior divisions ignore the grid. The corrected contract: give each card a span so that every interior edge lands on a track start, and keep the spans in the same small vocabulary the rest of the page uses.

checks.check: Every card edge lands on a track start or end
Cards are placed by span, not sized by content
Card widths bear a stated ratio to one another rather than an arbitrary one
The card row uses the same grid definition as the section label above it
The row is flush to both rails and its interior divisions respect tracks

evidence: measured card boxes at 1440: card 1 x 40 w 558.8; card 2 x 598.8 w 457.9; card 3 x 1056.7 w 343.3 — widths 559 / 458 / 343
card 2's x 598.8 sits 1.2px from the column-9 start (600) — within a gutter, not on a track
card widths ratio: card 1 is 1.63x card 2; card 3 is 0.75x card 2
each card carries padding '0px 16px' and no background, border or radius; the images inside are the only visual

parts.name: Cards share a baseline for their images
parts.description: This is a second negative move. The three cards are equal height, but their images begin at three different vertical positions — 4238.1, 4321.9 and 4410.4px — a spread of 172.3px, because each card's text above the image takes a different number of lines and the image simply floats below it. The visible result is a stepped row where the eye expects a common top.
parts.entry_test: Not a gesture to copy — the opposite. A row of parallel cards must align on a shared internal edge; here the staggering of the images is the defect.
parts.recipe: Fix the internal order so the image occupies a consistent band. As authored, the meta line and headline sit above the image and their height varies with the text (card 1's title block is 55.9px tall, card 2's 12.7px, card 3's 34.3px), pushing each image down by a different amount. The corrected contract: either place the image first in every card, or give the text block above it a fixed height, so that all card images share a common top edge and the cards' internal rhythm is identical. Note the spread measured here is 172.3px — nearly a third of a card's height.

checks.check: All card images share a common top edge
The element order inside each card is identical
Any text block above an image has a fixed, not content-derived, height
Cards are equal height and their internal bands line up
The image's own aspect is consistent across cards

evidence: measured image tops: 4238.1, 4321.9, 4410.4 — a spread of 172.3px across three cards in one row
measured card tops are identical (all 4079.3) and card heights identical (all 570.8) — the misalignment is internal, not row-level
element order is the same (meta 4079.3, title 4106.7, image below) but the title block heights differ: 55.9 / 12.7 / 34.3px
rendered image widths differ: 632.2, 511.1, 392.8 — the images match their cards' content widths, not a shared track

parts.name: Metadata rail subordinate to the measure
parts.description: The date sits in the rail directly above the share controls, in the body size and weight, with no heading treatment. The rail is a single narrow stack of small items that never competes with the article's opening.
parts.entry_test: Headline the rail and it competes with the article; the flat treatment is what keeps the metadata readable but secondary.
parts.recipe: A 156px rail on columns 1-2 holding the date line in body type and a stack of share controls beneath it. The rail is authored to travel with the scroll (it is inside a sticky wrapper; its box measures 1732px against the article's 1044px content height). Keep the rail's type at or below body size, use no heading weight, and do not let the rail's controls take a container, background or border.

checks.check: The rail holds metadata and controls only, no body text
Rail type is at or below body size with no heading treatment
The rail stays narrower than half the article measure
Share controls are borderless and unfilled
The rail is sticky against the scroll rather than static

evidence: measured rail box x 40 y 2166.2 w 156 h 1732; article content x 384 w 672 h 1044
rail contents: 'Published October 2 2026' plus controls labelled Copy Link, Facebook, LinkedIn, X
control computed: background rgba(0,0,0,0), border '0px none', border-radius 0px, padding 0px
rail is 156px against the article's 672px — 23% of the measure

parts.name: Two families, one ratio, percentage tracking
parts.description: The page uses two type families only — a display face for headlines and a text face for everything else — with a constant 5:1 ratio between display and body size. Tracking is a fixed percentage of font size rather than a per-size value: -3% everywhere, with one documented exception at the smallest size.
parts.entry_test: Break the ratio and the page's voice splits between a shout and a whisper; the 5:1 relationship held across every breakpoint is what makes one scale work at 390 and at 1440.
parts.recipe: Two families: jobyDisplay for display sizes, jobyText for body and UI. Sizes in use: 80px/550 display, 64px/550 section heading, 24px/500 summary, 20px/500 item titles, 18px/450 links, 16px/400 body, 14px/450 captions, 12px/450 labels. Tracking is -3% of the font size (80 -> -2.4, 64 -> -1.92, 24 -> -0.72 at display tracking, 18 -> -0.36, 16 -> -0.32); the single exception is the 12px size, which uses -2% (-0.24). Display line-height is 1.0; body line-height is 1.4. The display-to-body ratio holds at 5.0 across breakpoints — 80:16 at 1440 and 65.16:13.03 at 834.

checks.check: Exactly two type families are used
Tracking is a fixed percentage of size rather than a per-size value
Display line-height is tight (1.0) and body line-height is open (1.4)
The display-to-body ratio holds across breakpoints
No uppercase transform and no weight outside the defined set

evidence: families present: jobyDisplay and jobyText only (plus fallbacks)
computed: h1 80px/550, line-height 80px (1.0), letter-spacing -2.4px; section h2 64px/550, line-height 64px, letter-spacing -1.92px
computed: body p 16px/400, line-height 22.4px (1.4), letter-spacing -0.32px; summary 24px/500, line-height 28.8px, letter-spacing -0.24px
weights in use: 400, 450, 500, 550 — half-hundred steps, none bold, none below 400

parts.name: Quotations set as body text
parts.description: This is a third negative move. The article contains two quoted passages — one from a company executive — but there is no blockquote element and no quotation styling: the quotes run as ordinary 16px body paragraphs in the text face, distinguished only by curly quotation marks. A long attributed quotation therefore reads as one more paragraph.
parts.entry_test: Not a gesture to copy — the opposite. An attributed quotation is a distinct element and should be marked as one.
parts.recipe: Mark quotations as quotations. On this page the quoted paragraphs compute identically to every other paragraph — 16px/400 in jobyText inside the 672px measure, no blockquote, no indentation, no rule, no size change, no attribution line. The corrected contract: give a quotation its own element and a treatment that separates it from body text — a size or face change, an indent or rule, and an attribution set in the caption style. The quote must remain readable at the article measure but must not be mistakable for a body paragraph.

checks.check: An attributed quotation is marked by a distinct element or treatment
A quotation is visually separable from body paragraphs
An attribution is present and set in the caption style
A quotation does not set at the same size, face and weight as body text
Any quotation treatment keeps the article's measure

evidence: zero blockquote elements exist in the document
the two quoted paragraphs compute identically to the other four: 16px/400, line-height 22.4px, letter-spacing -0.32px, jobyText, x 384 w 672
no quotation was found with a size above 28px outside the headline, summary and section heading
quotations open with a curly quote character inside otherwise ordinary paragraph markup

parts.name: Images fade in after their placeholder
parts.description: Every image on the page carries a two-part entrance: a placeholder element that holds for 400ms, then the image itself fading in over 400ms on a decelerating curve. The image is never visible in its unloaded state.
parts.entry_test: Load the images straight in and the page flashes unloaded boxes; the placeholder-then-fade sequence is what keeps the layout calm while the media arrives.
parts.recipe: Two animations per image: a placeholder with duration 0ms and delay 400ms, and the image itself with duration 400ms, delay 0, easing cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1) (an ease-out). Combine them with a fadeIn keyframe (opacity 0 to 1). Keep the total under 800ms and never let an image animate its size — only its opacity.

checks.check: Images fade in rather than appearing instantly
A placeholder holds before the image appears
The entrance uses a decelerating curve
Only opacity animates, never size or position
The whole entrance completes within about 800ms

evidence: captured animations on the media image: placeholder node duration 0ms delay 400ms; image node duration 400ms delay 0 easing cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1)
the page's shared keyframe library defines fadeIn as opacity 0 to 1
the same two-part pattern repeats on every image in the page (three news cards carry it as well)

parts.name: A small named easing set
parts.description: Easing is declared as named custom properties on the root rather than written inline per component, and the set is small: a symmetric in-out for surfaces, a decelerating out for arriving content, and a standard link transition. The same values drive the nav, the cards and the footer.
parts.entry_test: Scatter inline cubic-bezier values through components and the page's motion stops feeling like one system; the shared tokens are what make an unrelated nav and footer move with the same hand.
parts.recipe: Declare the easing set on :root and consume it everywhere: --ease-in-out-cubic cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1); --ease-out-cubic cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1); --link-transition transform .3s cubic-bezier(.165,.84,.44,1). Content that arrives uses the out curve; surfaces that open use the in-out curve; link underlines use the 300ms link transition. Do not author new curves per component.

checks.check: Easing values are declared as shared tokens, not inline per component
Arriving content uses a decelerating curve
Opening surfaces use a symmetric in-out curve
The easing set stays small
The same tokens are reused across unrelated components

evidence: resolved on :root: --ease-in-out-cubic cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1); --ease-out-cubic cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1); --link-transition transform .3s cubic-bezier(.165,.84,.44,1)
the media image entrance uses the out curve; the 'View all News' control transitions colour over 0.3s on the same out curve
the nav and footer share the same token names, confirming one motion system across the page

parts.name: Dark ink on cream, with three flat accents
parts.description: The page is built on a near-black ink and a warm off-white canvas — those two tokens account for almost all text and background on the page. Against them sit three flat accent colours used in single occurrences each, with no gradients anywhere in the body.
parts.entry_test: Add a gradient or a fourth accent and the page's colour stops reading as a system of flat tokens; the discipline is that accents appear once each.
parts.recipe: Two dominant tokens: ink rgb(14,22,32) for all text and the near-white canvas rgb(245,244,223) for the page and the Read next band. Three accents, each occurring once: brand blue rgb(0,122,229) on the footer link field, deep navy rgb(28,63,153) on the footer's closing band, orange rgb(235,97,16) as a single band below it. Reversed text is the same near-white token on the blue surfaces. No gradients anywhere in the body; the only large colour surfaces are flat fills.

checks.check: One ink and one canvas token carry nearly all text and background
Accent colours are flat fills, never gradients
Reversed text uses the same light token as the canvas
No gradient appears in the body of the page
Accents are used sparingly rather than spread across surfaces

evidence: resolved tokens: --color-blue #007ae5, --color-dark-blue #1c3f99, --color-orange #eb6110, --color-pink #ffd9c9
the footer link field is the brand blue and its closing band the deep navy — both flat fills
no linear-gradient or radial-gradient resolves on any body element

parts.name: Headline that holds its scale down the page
parts.description: The headline is set at 80px with tight leading (line-height equal to font size) and negative tracking, spanning 12 of 16 columns. Its block is 456.3px tall against a 713.1px hero band, so the headline plus its metadata fill the band without crowding.
parts.entry_test: Open the leading and the headline stops reading as a single mass; the 1.0 line-height is what lets 80px type stack without gaps.

parts.name: Links marked by a rule that draws in

limitations:
Paragraph spacing is a defect, not a target. The page separates paragraphs with
elements (each 19px, one line-height), producing a 38px gap that is two line-heights. The rubric requires a declared margin instead. This is recorded as negative evidence.

The card row is a defect, not a target. Cards are sized by content (559 / 458 / 343px) rather than by span, so card 2 starts at x 598.8 — between tracks. The corrected contract requires placement by span.

The card image misalignment is a defect, not a target. Image tops spread 172.3px (4238.1 / 4321.9 / 4410.4) because each card's text above the image takes a different number of lines. The rubric requires a shared image top edge.

The absent quotation treatment is a defect, not a target. The page contains quoted passages but no blockquote element and no quotation styling, so a long attributed quotation reads as body text. The rubric's 'display face in body' move is the author's corrected contract and is flagged as not present on the source.
Card aspect ratios are inconsistent (1.41, 1.43, 1.50) and the rubric records this as a defect rather than a target value.
The hero image's 202.5px vertical offset is confirmed as a measurement but whether it is authored composition or an artifact of object-position was not resolved.
Which element owns the media band's 1.6:1 aspect was not isolated — the section is 900px tall against 1440 wide, while the image itself renders at 1.39:1 and is cropped.

Motion at 834 and 390 was not sampled per element; the entrance values come from the 1440 pass and from the page's shared keyframe library. The stagger across the three news cards is inferred, not measured.
Hover and focus states on body links and the rail controls were read from authored CSS; only the 'View all News' colour transition was captured live.
The sidebar rail's sticky behaviour was not exercised by scrolling; it is described from its box dimensions and the sticky wrapper in the markup.
The characters-per-line estimate of 84 is a calculation from the measure and a nominal average character width, not a count of actual line breaks.
The article's word count (about 290) is an estimate from line counts and measure, not an exact token count.
The 'View all News' control's accessible name is duplicated in the markup ('View all News View all News'). Recorded as a copy defect; whether it renders duplicated to a screen reader was not tested.
The nav and footer are site-wide components with their own rubrics; they are described here only as they appear on this page and are not re-graded.
